chunks: Will he who has a clear proof from his Lord, which acts as evidence from Him, before which the Book of Moses was a way-giver and a grace, (not believe in it)? Whoever among the partisans does not believe in it shall have Hell as the promised award. So have no doubt about it, for surely it's the truth from your Lord, though most men may not believe.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Book of Moses in relation to the Quranic revelation in Surah Hud?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'clear evidence' (bayyinah) and the 'witness' (shahid) are often interpreted as the Prophet Muhammad and his progeny, the Ahl al-Bayt, who embody the continuity of divine guidance. The reference to the Book of Moses highlights the principle of tawatur and the unbroken chain of revelation, affirming the Prophet's authority through prior scriptures. This verse underscores the inevitability of truth despite the majority's disbelief, a key theme in Shia eschatology regarding the eventual triumph of the faithful.
